question: Look-through sector shares: follow top-50 DAF dollars one hop past the 10 core pass-through intermediaries (3 fiscal sponsors, 5 pooled funds, 2 grantmaking public charities) by allocating each one's FY2023-24 top-50 inflow pro rata over its own Schedule I Part II and Part IX line 3 outflows, then recompute the NTEE sector shares in daf-grant-recipient-sectors-top50.csv on a look-through basis
conclusion_affected: Sector shares of DAF dollars (the core intermediaries take $1.77bn, 2.26% of top-50 non-D2D dollars, and are coded C/T/U/P by their own NTEE rather than by what they fund)
rationale: The 10 regrant 86% of contributions within the two tax years (Part IX lines 1-3 / Part VIII 1h) and $183m moves between members of the set (e.g. Climate Imperative to Energy Foundation China $56.8m), so their NTEE code says little about the end use of the DAF dollars they take

question: Is Bright Funds Foundation (EIN 46-2109112) a DAF sponsor or a donation processor? Read its FY2023-24 990 Schedule D Part I, Part IV line 6 and public product pages; if it holds donor-advised or donor-directed accounts, test it against the DAF-to-DAF whitelist rules (W1-W4)
conclusion_affected: DAF-to-DAF exclusion ($72.4m from Vanguard Charitable FY2023-24 is currently counted as a final charity grant)
rationale: It receives $72.5m from 3 top-50 sponsors (99.9% from one), regrants 92% of contributions, files Part IX grants with no Schedule I Part II lines, and its homepage redirects to a workplace-giving product site; Part IV line 6 is 0 in both years, which does not settle whether it runs donor-directed funds

question: Purpose text of top-50 lines to New Venture Fund, Hopewell Fund and Windward Fund: read PurposeOfGrantTxt on the 136 FY2023-24 lines from each filer's Schedule I XML and classify them as project-named, generic, or general support of the sponsor, as was done for Assets Under Movement in g050303-02
conclusion_affected: How much of the $662m that the three fiscal sponsors take is earmarked to named projects; recall of the de facto fiscal-sponsor detector (P-G050303-01)
rationale: Hopewell's own page says 'Projects raise their own funding', so DAF grants to the sponsor EIN are probably project-directed, but the recipient name field rarely says so (g0503-03 found 2 project-style lines to NVF and Windward and none to Hopewell)

question: Timing reconciliation for the 6 EINs where top-50 DAF dollars exceed the recipient's own Part VIII 1h / 990-PF contributions over tax years 2023-24 (Breakthrough Energy Catalyst, Connecticut Project, Homewise, Primary School, Worthington Scholarship Foundation, XQ Institute): add tax years 2022 and 2025 and the program-service revenue lines, and match each sponsor line to the recipient year by sponsor fiscal-year end
conclusion_affected: Onward-flow ratios and DAF-share-of-contributions for small-filer recipients; daf-share-of-recipient-revenue share_gt_100pct
rationale: Connecticut Project shows $30.0m from Fidelity Charitable against $12,496 of filed contributions, and Breakthrough Energy Catalyst $60.0m from The Chicago Community Trust against $2.6m, so the money sits in another year or another revenue line

question: Correct the donate-page scan's home_only_no_donate_link category: re-scan the rows whose homepage redirects to another host (UCLA Foundation to mygiving.ucla.edu; Bright Funds to hello.brightfunds.org) or that have an unlinked /donate page (Homewise), following the redirect host's own robots.txt
conclusion_affected: The 28-row 'no donate link' group in nonprofit-donate-page-daf-scan-2026.csv, and the share of top-300 DAF recipients that offer a DAF option
rationale: 3 of the 28 rows are scan artefacts rather than organisations without a giving page; the scan treated an off-host redirect as the homepage and read only links, not common paths

question: Sponsor-side routing rules for grants to fiscal sponsors and pooled funds: collect the public help-centre text of the top-10 sponsors on (a) recommending a grant to a fiscally sponsored project (designation field, written agreement), (b) grants to donor collaboratives with minimum commitments, and (c) how such grants are paid (check, ACH, wire)
conclusion_affected: How DAF money reaches recipients with no donate page; the 'sponsor portal only' finding for the named intermediaries
rationale: None of the 10 core intermediaries publishes a donate page, DAF instructions, wire details or its EIN on the public pages read, so the receiving path is set by the sponsor (grant recommendation and sponsor-initiated payment) and only sponsor documents can describe it
